amendment.change: Non-finite daily correlations are treated as missing in v2; no strategy or gate change.
amendment.reason: Preflight v1 aggregation produced NaN correlations after the new gate shrank some daily candidate sets.

classification: fixed agreement gate on C-sleeve candidates; original C score and all portfolio rules frozen
diagnostics: Report the 2022 partial return and drawdown versus R344 control
Report 5x top1/top3/top5 net contribution versus R344 control
Report C standalone return and drawdown as diagnostic only; portfolio gates remain authoritative
Report factor contribution and holdings overlap with the control C sleeve
discipline: One fixed agreement gate; do not scan the 0.6 rank threshold, minimum agreement count, component set, C score weights or risk-budget rules
No paper target or order file
Use historical membership, T+1 open execution and the system StrategyBacktestService
The gate is frozen before returns
disclosure: The factor and strategy files were written before any portfolio return, drawdown, trade or concentration result was computed. Preflight v1 failed only on NaN correlation aggregation before returns; v2 maps non-finite daily correlations to null and passes all coverage checks. No strategy, gate, threshold or window changed between v1 and v2.
economic_rationale: The gate requires agreement >=2 among momentum, quality-value, cash-quality and low-vol ranks. It is a nonlinear candidate constraint, not a weight change: the original 40/25/20/15 C score is retained. Preflight v2 has 83,425 candidate rows, 1,090 days, mean 76.5 candidates/day, and maximum mean comparator correlation 0.3187.

hypothesis: Removing C-sleeve candidates that rank above the 60th percentile in fewer than two of four dimensions reduces single-factor extremes and broadens net-profit generation enough to improve 2022 and 5x concentration without degrading long-window return or drawdown.
known_limitations: The gate is derived from the same four sleeves and is not an independent data source.
A 2-of-4 agreement threshold is a fixed economic rule, not an optimized parameter.
Financial firms are handled by existing C-sleeve filters rather than separate treatment.
Current-snapshot industry classification is backfilled through history.
Membership is reconstructed and ETF qfq is not official PIT total return.
The common window starts in 2022 because TTM financial factors are unavailable earlier.
The 10% C cap and gold trend rule were selected in prior post-hoc research.
Candidate breadth under the gate averages 76.5 names/day but has a minimum of 1, which can create concentration on sparse days.
